title: throughput-safeguards-service-level-definition-and-budgeting
creator: Elena Morales
description: Draft a throughput-focused SLA definition, error budget calculus, and contract-ready language for Reserved/Dedicated capacity customers. The goal is a measurable, auditable definition of throughput guarantees that aligns engineering enforcement (autoscaling/fleet controls), finance credits mechanics, and legal contract language. Avoid vague phrasing; provide deterministic formulas and remediation tiers.
objectives: 1) Define a throughput availability SLO that is implementable by the runtime and verifiable in telemetry. 2) Create an error budget model tied to time-weighted throughput shortfalls and translatable to credits. 3) Produce contract language and a short annex that legal can drop into MSAs and order forms. 4) Coordinate with ENG on enforcement/debug hooks and with Sales on examples for quoting.
proposed_sla_definition: Throughput Availability (TA) = 1 - (Sum over measurement windows of shortfall_minutes / total_minutes) where a measurement window is 5 minutes and shortfall_minutes counts minutes within a window where observed sustained throughput < committed_throughput * (1 - tolerance). Committed_throughput is expressed as tokens/sec or requests/sec in the order form. Tolerance defaults to 5% for measurement smoothing. TA is reported monthly; an SLA is met when monthly TA >= 99.5% for Standard and >= 99.95% for Premium tiers.
error_budget_calculation: Monthly error budget (minutes) = total_minutes_in_month * (1 - SLA_target). When shortfall occurs, decrement error_budget by shortfall_minutes weighted by severity multiplier: 1.0 for full shortfall (observed < 80% of committed), 0.5 for partial shortfall (80-95%), 0.25 for marginal (95-99%). If error_budget <= 0, remediation tiers trigger. Example: For SLA_target 99.5% in a 30-day month, monthly budget = 30*24*60*0.005 = 216 minutes.
remediation_playbook: Tier 0 (informational): automated alert to account owner and ops when shortfall detected. Tier 1 (engineering response): if rolling shortfall > 30 minutes or severity multiplier 1.0, engage on-call runtime team to investigate autoscaling/queueing. Tier 2 (service credit): when monthly error_budget exhausted, issue service credit equal to credit_rate * (minutes_exhausted) where credit_rate is defined in the order form (default 0.1% of monthly bill per 60 minutes exhausted, capped at 50% of monthly bill). Tier 3 (contractual remedies): repeated SLA failures across two consecutive months escalate to executive review and potential termination rights per contract annex. All incidents require a postmortem within 10 business days explaining root cause, mitigation, and timeline for recurrence prevention.
autoscaling_and_fleet_controls_alignment: To make the SLA enforceable, define enforcement knobs: 1) Reserved pool headroom: Dedicated pools will maintain a configurable headroom percentage (default 15%) to accommodate scale bursts. 2) Burst allowances: customers may purchase burst credits for sustained bursts above committed throughput for N minutes per month. 3) Autoscaling policy requirements: contract requires a minimum autoscaling rapidness (scale-up latency target) of 90s for x% increase in load; if provider autoscaling exceeds this, it contributes to shortfall. 4) Fallback routing: specify prioritized fallback models/regions and associated impact to throughput guarantees.
contract_language_snippets: 1) Service Commitment: 'Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to provide the Committed Throughput described in the Order Form. Throughput Availability (TA) is defined and measured as described in the Throughput Availability definition in Annex A.' 2) Credits: 'If Redwood fails to meet the Commitment in a Billing Month such that Customer's Monthly Error Budget is exhausted, Customer will be eligible for a Service Credit calculated per the Error Budget and Credit Rate in the Order Form.' 3) Measurement & Disputes: 'Redwood's telemetry will be the primary source of measurement. Customer may open a dispute within 30 days of the billing end date; both parties will review the raw telemetry and a joint adjustment may be applied.'
acceptance_criteria: SLA math expressed in deterministic formulae and examples (worked 30-day and 31-day months)
Error budget examples with severity weighting and credit calculation for Standard and Premium tiers
Annex A draft suitable for legal review and copy/paste into MSA (<= 800 words)
Engineering sign-off on required telemetry hooks and autoscaling signals (list of metrics and webhooks)
Sales-approved sample order form lines and billing examples for quoting

Week 3: draft Annex A and contract snippets and circulate to Legal/Sales (Mar 1-7). Week 4: engineering implementation plan and telemetry spec ready for ENG sprint (Mar 8-15). Target: legal-ready SLA annex by 2026-03-15.
open_questions: Should committed_throughput be allowed as a blended metric (tokens/sec for generation + requests/sec for classification)?
What is the default tolerance percent (we propose 5%) and when should we permit customer-negotiated tolerances for large enterprises?
Do we need a separate, simpler SLO for short-lived bursts (e.g., burst minutes allowance) vs sustained throughput?
How should credits interact with committed overage billing when we automatically route to burst capacity?
implementation_notes_for_engineering: Telemetry: emit per-customer 5m window summary metrics: committed_throughput, observed_throughput, shortfall_minutes, severity_bucket. Provide a read-only endpoint for monthly SLA report and raw telemetry export for disputes. Autoscaler: add event markers when scale actions are initiated/completed and include queue depth metrics; expose webhooks for critical escalation. Fleet controls: enable headroom configuration per pool and a burst-credits metering mechanism.
